# ADR-0005: Articles revise in place; re-fetch only through the repair queue

## Status

Accepted (2026-07-10, not yet implemented).

## Decision

Re-acquiring the same URL with materially changed content updates the same article as `revision + 1`; it never creates a new article. Old revision bodies are retained and stay dereferenceable (labeled superseded); search indexes only the latest revision. Automatic re-fetching happens only for quality-flagged acquisitions (suspected truncation or extraction damage) through a repair queue drained by the next Scan, plus a manual refresh command. What forced this: acquisition was one-shot (`fetched_urls` gates a URL forever), so truncated extractions could never heal, and nothing schema-level prevents same-URL duplicate rows once re-fetching exists.

## Considered options

- Automatic second-look re-fetch of every article after 24-48h: rejected, roughly doubles browser-quota spend on mostly unchanged pages.
- Manual refresh only: rejected, in practice truncations would never get repaired.

## Consequences

- Revision comparison uses normalized bodies, so whitespace-level scrape noise cannot mint revisions.
- One row per URL becomes schema-enforced.
- Live-blog articles are exempt: their mutability is per Live update, not per revision.

3:The acquisition and retrieval half of the system's feed capability. It scrapes a fixed set of Providers for articles and live-blog updates, persists them, and serves them to consumers through `feedq`. It is the source of truth for acquired feed source material and its retrieval indexes, and for nothing else: notes, truth, verification, vendor facts, roster relevance, and memory live in other contexts. LLM-driven work of any kind (extraction, classification, validation, clustering, synthesis, enrichment) is out of scope here. The identity, revision, and chunk vocabulary below is decided language (ADR-0004 through ADR-0010, accepted 2026-07-10) that implementation is still catching up to: today `feedq` serves article-grain BM25 and still prints internal ids.
17:One end-to-end acquisition run over a date range. A Scan visits each selected Provider's listings, collects article links, extracts content for new links, discovers Live updates, and (once ADR-0005 lands) drains the Repair queue. A Scan is the unit of idempotency: re-running over the same range re-checks but does not re-extract unchanged articles.
21:One acquired piece of feed content (title, summary, clean body text, publication metadata). Publicly identified by its Article ref; its text advances through Revisions. The internal `content_hash` (SHA-256 of the first 2,000 characters of the cleaned body; absent for very short bodies) drives dedup and is never a public identity.
